original_question: For the groups SL_n(F_p), and more generally for finite simple groups of Lie type, is there a uniform positive lower bound on the cocycle Cheeger constants in permutations for the expansive Steinberg presentations, at least when n is fixed and p tends to infinity? Conversely, do the cocycle Cheeger constants in permutations for the much shorter Guralnick-Kantor-Kassabov-Lubotzky presentations necessarily tend to zero when either n or p tends to infinity?
target_in_paper: Section 6.4, Conjecture 6.7: the shortness-versus-stability conjecture for the Steinberg and Guralnick-Kantor-Kassabov-Lubotzky (GKKL) presentations of SL_n(F_p), and more generally groups of Lie type. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2311/2311.06706v3.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact target: it identifies the two presentation families singled out in Section 6.4, it asks for a uniform positive lower bound for the Steinberg side in the regime 'fix n, let p tend to infinity,' and it asks for vanishing of the cocycle Cheeger constants for the GKKL side when n or p grows. That is essentially the content of Conjecture 6.7. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2311/2311.06706v3.pdf))
missing_details: The paper's invariant is specifically the dimension-1 cocycle Cheeger constant h1 of the associated presentation complex X_<S|R>, not an abstract group invariant independent of presentation. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2311/2311.06706v3.pdf))

'In permutations' means with permutation coefficients Sym and the normalized Hamming distance with errors; this metric is part of the formal definition of h1. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2311/2311.06706v3.pdf))

For a presentation <S|R>, the Cheeger constant depends on the chosen probability distributions mu_S and mu_R on generators and relations; the paper treats a presentation as equipped with such measures. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2311/2311.06706v3.pdf))

To make the Steinberg side stand-alone, one should recall the presentation the paper names: generators U_ij(a)=Id+e_ij(a) with relations U_ij(a)U_ij(b)=U_ij(a+b) and [U_ij(a),U_kell(b)]=1_{j=k}U_iell(ab). ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2311/2311.06706v3.pdf))

For the GKKL side, the paper does not spell out the full relations; what it records is their complexity: O(1) generators, O(1) relations, and relation length O(log n + log p). ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2311/2311.06706v3.pdf))

The nearby caveat in Remark 6.8 is omitted in the draft: the GKKL relation lengths are not uniformly bounded, which the paper says is unnatural from the property-testing viewpoint, though it still states Conjecture 6.7 for those presentations. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2311/2311.06706v3.pdf))

The surrounding scope is a concrete tradeoff question about presentation complexity versus stability for finite group presentations, not a broader conjecture about all presentations of finite simple groups. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2311/2311.06706v3.pdf))
refined_question: Let X_<S|R> be the presentation complex of a finite presentation <S|R>, equipped with its chosen probability measures on generators and relations, and let h1(X_<S|R>, Sym) denote its dimension-1 cocycle Cheeger constant with permutation coefficients Sym, computed using the normalized Hamming distance with errors. For the standard Steinberg presentation of SL_n(F_p) (more generally, of groups of Lie type), with generators U_ij(a)=Id+e_ij(a) and relations U_ij(a)U_ij(b)=U_ij(a+b) together with the usual Steinberg commutator relations [U_ij(a),U_kell(b)]=1_{j=k}U_iell(ab), is there a constant lambda>0 such that h1(X_Steinberg, Sym) >= lambda uniformly, at least in the regime where n is fixed and p tends to infinity? Conversely, for the Guralnick-Kantor-Kassabov-Lubotzky presentations of these groups, whose size is uniformly bounded and whose relation lengths are O(log n + log p), must h1(X_GKKL, Sym) tend to 0 along any family in which either n tends to infinity or p tends to infinity? ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2311/2311.06706v3.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, because h1(X, Sym)>0 is the same as linear cocycle stability in dimension 1, and a group presentation is homomorphism-stable in permutations exactly when its presentation complex is cocycle-stable in dimension 1, the question asks whether the Steinberg presentations admit a uniform linear homomorphism-stability rate in permutations in the fixed-n, p->infinity regime, while any linear rate for the GKKL presentations must degenerate as n or p grows. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2311/2311.06706v3.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting the right official statement: Section 6.4 first frames a tradeoff between short presentations and good stability, then highlights SL_n(F_p) and more generally groups of Lie type, describes the Steinberg and GKKL presentation families, and states Conjecture 6.7 in essentially the same two-part form as your draft. The main gap is that your version is not fully stand-alone in the paper's formal language, because it does not define h1 via the associated presentation complex, permutation coefficients, the normalized Hamming metric, or the dependence on generator/relation measures; it also omits the nearby Remark 6.8 caveat about unbounded GKKL relation length. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2311/2311.06706v3.pdf))
